narrative:
The model estimates an 80% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to employees who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your access to other job opportunities, your total years of experience across all roles, and the sector you work in. Having received other job offers while at the company was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving; most employees predicted to stay (77%) had not received such external offers, so this factor significantly raised your risk score. Your 6–10 years of overall experience also contributed toward leaving, as this range is less common among those expected to remain than shorter experience levels (50% of stayers have only 1–5 years). Finally, working in the “other” sector rather than medical or education pulled the prediction further toward departure, since that sector is underrepresented among employees the model expects to stay.

Taken together, these elements created a profile the model associates with higher turnover risk. The organization should discuss retention measures with you, such as clearer career paths or addressing any unmet needs, while you may want to reflect on whether your external opportunities better match your long-term goals. (218 words)
